searchText: incredible. i'd love to see the methodology behind this https://twitter.com/christine_dkim/status/1461346245004255283?s=20 the full report here: https://docsend.com/view/jngzufksntmpbgej They looked at people who offer for example 300 basefee, but ended up getting included for 150, saving them 150 in basefee, and voila, fee savings. But would they have bid 300 gwei in the first place if EIP1559 didnt exist? it's not a perfect measure, no true. but im of the opinion that EIP1559 leads to higher fees because an algorithm will never be as effecient as a free floating price, and the functionality that allows people to just put in a high bid and get some of it back encourages people to be more likely to overbid. in order to confirm the theory you would need to be able to objectively measure demand for transactions and compare it with fees pre and post EIP1559 which is not possible i think "efficient as free floating price" => free floating price isn't efficient at all. People don't know what to bid, as the volatility is high, so they overbid, and then they DON'T get refunded. "encourages people to be more likely to overbid" => so what? They are refunded anyway, so that the price they pay is fair. whatever
